threepl.codegen

Class TDEList

  • java.lang.Object
    • java.util.AbstractCollection<E>
      • java.util.AbstractList<E>
        • java.util.ArrayList<TDE>
          • threepl.codegen.TDEList
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    java.io.Serializable, java.lang.Cloneable, java.lang.Iterable<TDE>, java.util.Collection<TDE>, java.util.List<TDE>, java.util.RandomAccess, TDEConstants, Constant

    public class TDEList
extends java.util.ArrayList<TDE>
implements Constant, TDEConstants
    A TDE (Topological Description Element) list is the intermediate form of generated code. A TDE list has variable declarations at the front followed by logic using those variables. An index, 'variables', is used to maintain the insertion point for variables at the head of the list. Methods addTDE() append code TDEs to the tail of the list. Methods addVTDE insert TDEs at the end of the leading variable section of the list. Field 'index' provides a unique integer to append to the end of generated signal names. It is incremented after each use.

      • del

        public void del(TDEVar out,
                TDEVar in,
                TDEVar clock,
                TDEVar reset,
                QueueRefs pr)
        Create a delay TDE whose delay must be determined at the end of immediate execution and append it to the end of the TDElist. The QueueRef parameter is scanned for asynchronous unbuffered queues and if found the delay is set to 2, otherwise it is set to 1.
        Parameters:
        out - is the output signal
        in - is the input signal
        clock - is the clock input signal
        reset - input signal
        pr - is a queue reference which determines the delay required

      • del

        private void del(TDEVar out,
                 TDEVar in,
                 TDEVar clock,
                 int delay,
                 TDEVar reset,
                 QueueRefs pr)
        Create a fixed delay TDE or one whose delay may be determined at the end of immediate execution, and append it to the end of the TDElist. If the QueueRefs parameter 'pr' is null a fixed delay is created using the value supplied by parameter 'delay'. The QueueRef parameter 'pr', if not null, is scanned for asynchronous unbuffered queues and if found the delay is set to 2, otherwise it is set to 1. In this case parameter 'delay' is ignored.
        Parameters:
        out - is the output signal
        in - is the input signal
        clock - is the clock input signal
        delay - input signal
        reset - input signal
        pr - is a queue reference which determines the delay required

                    TDEVar ubqrpending,
                    SrcLoc loc)
        Conditionally generate a delayed start signal for a queue or priority wait. If the queue availability argument is null (no queue references) and pri_in is null (there is no enclosing priwait) simply return the start signal argument.
        Parameters:
        queues - is the queue references
        checkedqueues - is the queue references that have been checked already
        availok - true means that availability has already been checked and hence it is not necessary to check here
        scope - is the relevant variable scope
        sync - is true if this the control for a sync block
        start - is the start signal
        pri_in - is an optional input signal to a priority encoder
        pri_out - is an optional output signal from a priority encoder
        reset - is the reset input signal or null
        ubqwpending - is the unbuffered queue execution pending write output signal or null
        ubqrpending - is the unbuffered queue execution pending read output signal or null
        loc - is the source file location
        Returns:
        the TDE variable of the conditionally delayed start signal

        public void connect(TDEVar tdev,
                    Val val,
                    TDEVar exec,
                    java.lang.String mess,
                    SrcLoc loc)
        Connect a RHS value to a TDEVar. It is assumed that a type check has already been performed. Components will be expanded or truncated as required. This is only called from memRead() and memWrite() where exec signals are required.
        Parameters:
        tdev - is the TDEVar to be connected to
        val - is the value to connect to the TDEVar
        exec - is the execute signal
        mess - is an error message header
        loc - is the source file location

      • connect

        public void connect(TDEVar dtdevar,
                    TDEVar stdevar)
        Connect two TDEVars. If either argument is null or they are already connected, just return. Otherwise a CONNECT TDE is generated. If the two TDEVars are each complete, i.e. do not represent a part of a variable such as an array member or a struct field, then the CONNECT TDE may be optimised out later and the TDEVars merged (see method optimiseTDEList()).
        Parameters:
        dtdevar - sink TDEVar
        stdevar - source TDEVar

      • resolveDELs

        public void resolveDELs()
        Traverse the TDE list finding all DELs which wait on asynchronous unbuffered queues. The parameter of these is a QueueRefs class rather than an Integer. The parameter in that case is changed to an Integer whose value is 2 if the QueueRefs contains an asynchronous unbuffered queue, otherwise the value is 1.

      • optimiseTDEList

        public boolean optimiseTDEList(boolean continuous)
        Traverse the TDE list optimising some redundant TDEs. This optimisation is generic, not family-specific
        Parameters:
        continuous - if true finds any simple ILOOPs with one EXECP driving one DEL and removes the ILOOP, EXECP and DEl. The resulting start signal is now the avail input to the removed EXECP looped through pri_in and pri_out if they are non-null.
        Returns:
        true if the pass resulted in any changes
